# mabinogi-012 — review

## Pass 1 (2026-11-14)

All 73 units checked: note labels against the forms, `t` → `l` word by word, `l` ↔ `i`, house renderings,
consistency with 011, establishment-log coverage. Evans images viewed for col. 90 ll. 25–35 (daran, a'y taraw) and
col. 92 whole (bit bleidast, a gawssawch); Red Book (Rhŷs & Evans 1905, djvu text ll. 2540–2680) read for the whole
part. Edits made by script; no `t` touched (asserted).

### Changes

- 9 · l, i, n · major · yn diargel rendered 'openly' and glossed di- 'without' + argel. diargel is 'hidden, secret'
  (di- intensive), and the Red Book has yn dirgel; the sense is "done in secret, but I did not keep silent, so all
  the court knew" · l 'and that secretly', i 'and that in secret; but I did not keep silent', note rewritten.
- 13 · l, i, n · major · ar y bwyt a'y llynn taken as 'the food and the drink' with a'y = a'r. a'y is a + possessive
  'y; the Red Book's a'e can only be possessive · read 'his (Math's) food and his drink'; l, i and note changed.
- 20 · n · major · daran (doubt 1) said to "stand where yn might be expected". Image: Evans plainly *uẏd daran e6ic*;
  Red Book *yny uyd yndaran ewic*, i.e. yn daran ewic — daran is a separate word, it is yn that the White Book lacks
  · note rewritten (meaning unknown, left out of i; l keeps 'daran(?)').
- 20 · n · minor · uyd ← byd softened after yny not stated · added; also added that the Red Book has ae daraw (doubt 3).
- 71 · n · minor · "the Red Book has the same words" — the Red Book has *a uyryawd*, not *a uyrywys* (the log's
  statement was wrong); "son of Dôn, the smith" is not told in this text · corrected to the -awd ending; the
  outside-the-text identification removed.
- 72 · n · minor · "one of the Three Ill-fated Blows of the triads" claims a triad collection not verifiable here
  (doubt 10) · reworded "one of a set of three Ill-fated Blows"; the triad-formula reading of trydyd kept.
- 48 · n · minor · "though by the tale Hychdwn was borne by Gwydion" implied the verse contradicts the tale (doubt 9).
  By this part's own text: hind (Gilfaethwy) → Hyddwn; sow (Gwydion, ex-stag) → Hychdwn, with Gilfaethwy the boar;
  she-wolf (Gilfaethwy, ex-boar) → Bleiddwn. Borne by Gwydion is right, but all three are Gilfaethwy's · note restated.
- 48 · i · style · "three true champions" sounds remembered from a published translation; the note's 'champions or
  warriors' gloss was presented as "the usual guess" · i "three warriors true", note "a guess from the context".
- 53 · n · minor · "gawssawch in col. 93 above" — on the image a gawssawch is the last line of col. 92 · corrected.
- 11 · n · minor · Red Book quoted as "y2 hynn" (OCR r-rotunda) · "yr hynn".
- 11 · l · minor · uy iawn 'my amends' (amends are what Math owes Goewin; his own iawn is his redress; 011 uses
  'my right'/'my redress' for uy iawn) · l 'my redress'.
- 6 · n · minor · "the sentence before has Enteu Math" — that is two sentences back (unit 4) · corrected.
- 50 · l, n · minor · o bob un rendered 'to each one' (that is the Red Book's y bop un); bob ← pob unexplained ·
  l 'of each one'; note adds the mutation and the Red Book difference.
- 1 · n · minor · Guydyon/Gwydyon spellings (establishment log) not stated in any note · added.
- 21 · n · style · gwyduilot: mil → uil softening in the compound not named · added.
- 33 · n · style · y lleill for y naill (doubt 2) accepted; added that the Red Book has y lleill too.
- 42 · n · style · bit bleidast unsoftened (doubt 4) confirmed on the image (col. 92); added that the Red Book softens
  both (bit uleidast … bit uleid).

### Considered and refused

- Doubt 3, a'y taraw (20) vs A'y daraw (40): both confirmed on the images; the note's "unsoftened, as written" stands.
- Doubt 6, y am hynny (34) 'besides that': a defensible reading of y am 'from about, beyond'; the note already says
  the sense is not certain. Kept.
- Doubt 7, Canys ywch yn rwymedigaeth: ywch is the 2 pl. present of bot (as yd ywch in the same speech); 'since you
  are under bond' is right. Kept.
- Doubt 8: carnen 'sow' is fixed by the tale (the sow's son is Hychdwn, from hwch) — kept; crynllwdyn 'a fine young
  one' and braswineu 'sturdy and auburn-haired' are built from the parts and hedged in the notes — kept;
  kenryssedat — i changed only in wording (above).
- 34 i avoids naming who heard ("there came the baying") because clywyn is a slip of uncertain intent: right. Kept.
- 44 t has y'r dyd where Evans prints *ẏ2 dẏd* (= yr): an establishment matter, not a unit fault; `t` not touched.
  Flag for the establisher if wanted.
- 4/7 column claims (Caer Tathyl col. 86; Goewyn col. 87, Goewin col. 82) agree with 011's published notes. Kept.
- 1 "the hostage Gwrgi Gwastra of the last part": verified in 011. Kept.
- 6 "ym plyc croth, as in part 011": verified (011 ymlyc croth). Kept.
- 5 "the circuit Gilfaethwy made for Math in part 011": 011 has Gilfaethwy and Eufydd y gylchu y wlat drostaw. Kept.
- 46 crubothon "a word found only here", 48 kenryssedat "not found elsewhere in this form": standard hedged
  statements, not claims about other parts. Kept.
- 59 camu 'bend' / camu 'step' wordplay: offered as possible, not asserted. Kept.
- 72 i "one of the Three Ill-fated Blows": the triad formula reading is sound; kept.
- House renderings (heb ef/heb ynteu, Ie, Sef dropped in i, a oruc folded, teulu, kyuoeth, kerennyd), hutlath
  'magic-rod'/'magic rod', iawn, Gwydion, Gilfaethwy, Caer Dathyl, Goewin: all consistent. No change.

## Pass 2 (glossary) (2026-11-14)

I checked all 128 new entries in `gloss.json` and all 30 `__broaden__` entries against the text and the pass-1 units.
I also checked every known form in `known-forms.json` against this part's uses. Edits were made by script. Each broaden
was checked to start with its old entry whole, followed by " · ". Every `novel-forms.json` key still has a non-empty
entry (script check: 128/128). No `t` was touched.

### Changes

- benelinyaw · gloss · major · lemma given as "penlinio (penelinio) — to kneel (from penn-glin 'knee')". It is
  penelinyaw (penelinio) 'lean on the elbow, recline', from penelin 'elbow' · rewritten. The broadened entries for y
  and lle repeated 'kneel' and now say 'recline'.
- diargel · gloss · major · glossed 'not hidden, open', "sense likeliest 'openly'". This is against pass 1: the word
  means 'hidden, secret' and the Red Book has yn dirgel · rewritten to 'secretly'.
- chamu · gloss · major · glossed 'to step … her stepping (it)'. a'y chamu is 'and bent it': camu 'bend', with 'y
  'it' (the hutlath, feminine) · rewritten, and the step/bend pun noted.
- enneint · gloss · major · glossed 'ointment, unguent'. Middle Welsh enneint is 'bath' (pass-1 note, unit 50) ·
  rewritten. perwch's example also had 'ointments' and was corrected.
- chrynllwdyn · gloss · major · glossed 'plump young pig, piglet', with cryn given as 'round, small'. cryn means
  'considerable, fair-sized', so the sense is a well-grown young beast · rewritten.
- hydwn · gloss · major · said Hyddwn was "born as a boar-pig". He is the fawn of the first year, borne by
  Gilfaethwy as the hind · rewritten.
- gnotayssynt · gloss · major · "gn- is unmutated or a mutation of cn-, uncertain" is an invented mutation. gnotau
  (gnotáu) is radical · rewritten.
- bethan · gloss · major · lemma "bethan (bethan)", radical. It is pethan (peth + -an), softened after ryw · rewritten
  as noun m.
- trillydyn / eodynt · gloss · major · glossed 'a trio, a set of three young beasts … three of a kind'. It is tri +
  llydyn 'three beasts' · rewritten. eodynt's example was corrected to match.
- daran · gloss · major · guessed taran 'thunder', soft-mutated after uyd. This is against pass 1, which says the
  meaning is unknown and the Red Book has yn daran · rewritten: meaning unknown, no mutation claimed, untranslated.
- berit · gloss · major · given as "impersonal preterite". It is the impersonal imperfect (-it) · corrected.
- dracheuyn · gloss · minor · lemma "dracheffyn" is invented, and "no mutation" contradicted the unit-0 note ·
  tracheuyn (trachefn, drachefn), softened in adverbial use.
- orawenus · gloss · minor · the etymology "gor- + gwenus" is wrong; it is gorawen 'great joy' + -us · corrected, and
  the mutation cause now matches the note.
- rydhaer · gloss · minor · given as "impersonal imperative". It is the impersonal present subjunctive used as a
  command (per the note) · corrected. rhyddhau was replaced by rydhau (rhyddhau).
- ellyngwyt · gloss · minor · "3 sg. impersonal" (an impersonal has no person) · corrected.
- wystlyssant · gloss · minor · glossed 'who gave hostages to us'. It is 'whom they pledged to us'; also gw>w is
  written as g lost · corrected.
- guypei · gloss · minor · given as "imperfect". It is the imperfect subjunctive (per the note) · corrected.
- threis · gloss · minor · "gender uncertain". treis/trais is m. · noun m.
- doethauch · gloss · minor · "d for dd, mutation not visible". The form is radical after y and after can ·
  corrected.
- gwyduilot · gloss · minor · "m of mil written u" did not name the mutation · soft mutation in the compound.
- atafi · gloss · minor · "at + fi". The pronoun is i · corrected.
- paret · gloss · minor · given as "noun f.". It is m. (y paret hwnn) · corrected.
- gymaredic · gloss · minor · lemma "cymharedig (uncertain; cf. cymharu 'compare')", 'matched'. It is kymaredic
  (cymharedig) 'mated, paired', from kymar · corrected.
- lleill · gloss · minor · "variant of y neill … perhaps by assimilation". lleill is the plural of llall used here for
  y naill (Red Book the same) · rewritten.
- clywyn · gloss · minor · "clywei likeliest" took a side that the note leaves open · now neutral.
- lydnot · gloss · minor · glossed 'brood, litter … collective'. It is plural of llwdn/llydyn, 'beasts' · rewritten.
- breisc · gloss · minor · lemma "breisg (breisg)" · breisc (braisg).
- braswineu · gloss · minor · glossed 'brown'. Corrected to 'auburn' (as in the unit); "lost in composition" now
  names the soft mutation.
- brasuelyn · gloss · minor · "m of melyn written u" · soft mutation named.
- bleidast · gloss · minor · "radical here" did not flag that it stands unsoftened after bit where soft mutation is
  expected · the Red Book's uleidast is now cited.
- enwir · gloss · minor · "following the plural noun … the wicked". It qualifies Giluaethwy ('Gilfaethwy the false')
  · corrected. Lemma enwir (anwir).
- chenryssedat · gloss · minor · "'chief men, true warriors'" · aligned with the unit: 'warriors' is a guess.
- chrubothon · gloss · minor · speculation on -on and the "parallel with crynllwdyn" removed · aligned with the note.
- rodwch · gloss · minor · lemma "rhodi (rhoi)" is an invented spelling · rodi (rhoddi, rhoi).
- gist · gloss · minor · glossed "(hand =) side of a chest", with the soft mutation said to come "after the feminine
  noun llaw (genitive)". It is the compound llaw gist 'hand-chest' · corrected. The llaw broaden had the same error
  and was rewritten.
- uyrywys · gloss · minor · "the lemma byryaw is old, uncertain" was garbled · bwrw, stem byry-, with the Red Book's
  a uyryawd noted.
- gouannon · gloss · minor · "the smith" is not told in this text (removed from the note in pass 1) · removed.
- ton, eil(broaden) · gloss · minor · "offspring/equal of Wave", "eil 'second, like'" · now 'second' or 'son,
  offspring', disputed, as in the note.
- ergyt · gloss · style · "a third unfortunate blow" · "the third ill-fated blow, one of three".
- uleid, bleid · gloss · style · lemma "blaidd (bleidd, blaidd)" · bleid (blaidd).
- yn (broaden) · gloss · minor · "yn y taraw wynteu 'then striking them' (y 'his')". y stands for eu 'their' (unit
  49) · corrected.
- y (broaden) · gloss · minor · ar y bwyt a'y llynn now cited as possessive 'his … his' (pass 1).
- ollwng (broaden) · gloss · minor · "noblemen" (singular in the text) and "subject after ynni" · corrected.
- gylchaw (broaden) · gloss · minor · "y 'to' … 'to go round Gwynedd'" did not match the note's 'round about' ·
  rewritten as y gylchaw 'round about' (the verbal noun after y used as a preposition).
- oet (broaden) · gloss · style · "sense uncertain" removed; the sense is plain ('for his age').
- hynny (broaden) · gloss · minor · "yn hynny 'thereupon'" · 'in that (time), meanwhile' (unit 13).
- tri · gloss (new broaden) · minor · the old entry said "no mutation", but here tri chenryssedat has a spirant
  mutation · broadened.
- etiued · gloss (new broaden) · minor · the old entry covered only 'heir'; here the word means 'offspring, young' of
  beasts · broadened.
- dowch · gloss (new broaden) · minor · the old entry covered only the present; here it is the imperative · broadened.
- e · gloss (new broaden) · minor · the old entry covered e 'his' only before a consonant; here it stands before a
  vowel and before h (e ystauell, e hutlath) · broadened.
- trydyd · gloss (new broaden) · minor · the triad formula was not covered · broadened.
- uchel · gloss (new broaden) · style · 'loud' was not covered · broadened.
- 44 · n · minor · per the coordinator: the note now says Evans writes yr as one word (the Red Book too), and that
  under our word division it is read y'r 'to the'.
- 7 · n · minor · the note had "weithon ← gweithon, softened as an adverb", which contradicts the published glossary
  entry (weithon always so written, gweith + hon) · the note was aligned with the glossary.

### Considered and refused

- ewyllwys "noun m.": the existing published entry for ewyllus says m.; left alone for consistency.
- hutlath: the gloss ('magic wand … sense disputed, magic wand likeliest') agrees with the unit-20 note. Kept.
- odorun/godorun: 'noise, disturbance', noun m., softened as the object, with g kept after the article. This agrees
  with unit 23. Kept.
- garnen/charnen: carnen 'sow', marked uncertain. The mutations (soft after bit, uu and yn; spirant after a) are
  right. Kept.
- gnotayssynt: the meaning is right; only the mutation was fixed (above).
- ergyt "gender uncertain (f. in later Welsh)" and diaspat m., traed/troed f.: GPC allows both genders, and the text
  gives no evidence. Kept.
- garw "soft … after uu": the predicate after bu is softened. Correct, kept.
- rwymedigaeth "unaffected by the nasal mutation after yn": rh takes no nasal mutation. Correct, kept.
- aranrot "Gwydion's sister": both are of Dôn in this text. Kept.
- caer "radical as object": a place-name; not worth a note. Kept.
- known forms that already cover this part (a, ar, uyd, uydant, gylch, cam, guelei, canys, dygyuor, guahard, adaw,
  mor, ymgueiraw, bwyt, llynn and the rest): no broaden needed.
